newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends sharply higher as market rebounds.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends sharply higher as market rebounds.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures raced higher Friday, surging nearly $50 in a sharp correction to the market's recent slide to life-of-contract lows.

In what traders and analysts said was primarily a technical correction from a severely oversold condition, the market retraced more than half its big six percent loss that was sustained over the past week.
Heavy shortcovering by speculators and industry buyers sent prices spiraling upward from virtually the opening bell, dealers said.
Benchmark March futures leapt $48 on the day to close at $1,308 a tonne, settling above the widely watched $1,300 barrier.
"It started the day oversold technically," said Smith Barney analyst Walter Spilka. "It was inevitably going to go up at some point."
Despite the market's recent wild ride, Spilka said the fundamental outlook for cocoa was little changed.

While early estimates for the 1996/97 crop in the Ivory Coast, the world's biggest producer, had called for a yield well below last year's record total, Spilka said the market's recent slump to 10-month lows indicated stockpiles were probably in good shape.
"The way the market acts, there is more cocoa out there than the numbers are showing," Spilka said. "The crop probably isn't going to come in a whole lot smaller than last year."
March futures traded widely from $1,265 to $1,313. Second-position May gained $44 to close at $1,339.
On the charts, traders said cocoa still had a while to go to shore up its stance. Key resistance was seen at $1,340 and $1,350, while support was pegged at $1,300 and in the low $1,280s.
The day's volume reached an estimated 10,956 lots.
((-- W Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
